EventItemActionText:
The Board of Architectural Review met in a regular session on Thursday, February 20,  2025, at 7:30 p.m. in Town Hall, 127 Center St S, Vienna, VA 22180.

Roll Call: Ms. Couchman, Ms. Shelly, Mr. Penati, Mr. O’Keefe, and Ms. Hanley were present. 

Staff present: Planner Sharmaine Abaied, and Board Clerk Yaska Camacho Castillo.

Item No. 1: Request for approval of exterior modifications to include outdoor seating, handrails, string lights, and awning - for Electric Bull, located at 176 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1610163-BAR, in the AC, Avenue Center zoning district, filed by Steve Kenney, RV Architects, project contact.

Applicant present: Steven Kenney 

Mr. Kenney discussed the outdoor furniture for the Electric Bull, an upscale steakhouse at the Vienna Shopping Center, which is taking over the old Cava space. They have chosen refined furniture, similar railings, and planters used in the rest of the center. The proposal also includes Tivoli lights, electric heaters, and an awning. Initially, a framed awning with posts was suggested, but the owner prefers a retractable awning. The awning fabric is black and fire-retardant-treated.

Mr. Penati asked if the retractable awning would remain closed most of the time and only be opened occasionally to which the applicant responded it would be used when needed, such as during high sun. It would extend out to the limits of the seating area. The existing storefront is 10 feet high, with a 2-foot bulkhead section. The awning will be mounted near the top, no lower than 7 feet, to avoid hitting people's heads.

Mr. O'Keefe asked the applicant if he had provided a rendering showing what the awning would look like when retracted. Mr. Kenney said he could provide one and mentioned that there are arms underneath some awnings, and recalled a previous approval for an awning at a new restaurant on Maple, which used Sunbrella fabric and was attached to the deck rail. He notes that the shopping center mostly has umbrellas, and the owner prefers a retractable awning that can be used occasionally rather than a permanent one. The awning in the rendering is shown projecting over just the seating area. The owner is also considering redoing the facade with a different color similar to another restaurant, but this is not part of the current review.

Mr. O’Keefe wondered about the proposed lighting and the applicant stated that the purpose for the lighting is to create an ambiance. If they go with the fixed awning the lights would be mounted along the periphery with a frame on the outer edge; for the non-fixed awning, the lighting would be mounted with I-hooks into the walls and supported by three posts. 

Ms. Hanley commented on the shopping center, noting that Taco Bamba and other nearby businesses share a similar style and color palette. While each business has its own set of furniture, there is continuity due to repeated use of planters and similar design elements. She feels this overlap creates a cohesive look. She also mentioned that if the applicant prefers, the design is fine, but she would like clarification on how the awning is attached to the wall, as the mounting detail has not been provided. 

Mr. Kenney responded that the awning would be bolted into the wall, which is double-framed. They will add blocking inside the inner bulkhead and through-bolt into it. The double-bolting is necessary to handle the stress on the wall. Ms. Hanley asked the applicant to provide the details he stated to staff as a follow-up item. 

There was a discussion about the awning height. Mr. Penati expressed concern that if the awning were lowered to seven feet, it might be within reach and could potentially be damaged additionally there is a potential for the metal bar to be misused as a pull-up bar, which could create an issue as well. Mr. Kenney said they will try to raise the awning as much as possible but they may be limited by the manufacturer's recommendation for that angle. He also noted that along the front edge of the retractable awning, there is a cover plate and a housing that holds the fabric. As the awning retracts, a bar pulls the fabric back, and when it closes, everything is encased, meaning the fabric isn't loose. 

Mr. O’Keefe felt that the awnings did not fit with the rest of the shopping center. Ms. Couhcman wondered what made the business owner propose retractable awnings. Mr. Kenney responded that they wanted something more upscale than simple umbrellas. 

There was a question about where the heaters would be mounted if retractable awnings were chosen. The applicant responded that they would be mounted underneath the bulkhead of the awning, to which Ms. Hanley pointed out that they would become more visible when the awning is retracted. 

After further discussion, Mr. O’Keefe stated that there were a few unanswered questions. Ms. Couchman asked if Architessa could be included in the project and if any changes are possible. She expressed regret that Mod Pizza and another restaurant can't switch locations so both could have an awning that stretches across the space. She feels that having an awning only on half of the yellowish-cream facade, with lights, might not be as aesthetically pleasing as having the awning stretch across the entire stretch, complementing the masonry columns. 

The applicant stated that he prefers the retractable awnings vs. the fixed awning because they are nicer and cleaner. He suggested that if the continuity of the design is a concern, they could divide the awning into two sections to align with the window frames below. He proposed placing one awning over the smaller window and another over the larger window on the right, as there’s no purpose in placing one on the left side since it wouldn’t be used. Ms. Couchman asked the applicant for architectural details for his proposal. 

There was a discussion about where to place lights, particularly focusing on whether to attach them to posts or railings. The applicant suggests that the lights should be on posts rather than railings due to practical reasons like tapping into existing structures and avoiding the use of skyhooks. He mentioned that on the near side, there is no nearby railing, so lights would need to be bolted into concrete. There's also a discussion about the desired ambiance, with the goal being a bistro-style look, meaning the lights should be higher up rather than down low to create a more atmospheric effect, as low-mounted lights wouldn't meet the intended ambiance.

After further discussion, the board members decided to separate the proposed items into two motions. 

Mr. O’Keefe made a motion to approve the application requesting exterior modifications that include the outdoor seating, and handrails and excludes the string lights, awning, and heating elements for the Electric Bull located at 176 Maple Ave W Docket No. PF-1610163-BAR, in the AC, Avenue Center zoning district, filed by Steve Kenney, RV Architects.

Motion: O’Keefe
Second: Sara
Motion Carried 

Mr. O’Keefe made a motion to defer the exterior modifications that include the string lights, awning, and heating elements for the Electric Bull located at 176 Maple Ave W Docket No. PF-1610163-BAR, in the AC, Avenue Center zoning district, filed by Steve Kenney, RV Architects.

Motion: O’Keefe
Second: Sara
Motion Carried 

For clarity purposes, the applicant asked the board to state what they are looking for. 
Ms. Couchman stated that they would like to see the architectural details for the neighboring restaurant Architessa with a retractable awning, lighting alternatives for the string lights, provide examples of how the retractable awning will look like when rolled up and with heaters,  the awning height specifications and awnings company specification sheet.
EventItemTitle: 176 Maple Ave W - Electric Bull - Outdoor Dining

Item No. 2: Request for approval of a wall sign, vinyl window clings, and a secondary sign for Clarity, located at 442 Maple Ave E, Docket No. PF-155195, in the AE, Avenue East zoning district, filed by Burton Francois, BeBold Sign Studio, project contact.

Applicant present:  No show 

The applicant was not present when the item was called at 8:06 pm. The item was moved to the bottom of the agenda.

Item No. 3: Request for approval of window signs for Panda Dumpling, located at 155 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1615945, in the AC, Avenue Center zoning district, filed by James Byars of Signs by James, LLC, project contact.

Applicant present: James Byars, Daniel (owner’s), and business owner. 

Mr. Byars stated that he was helping the tenant get a permit for the window signs. The signs are installed with vinyl graphics, featuring white lettering and some detailing. These vinyl pieces, which are peel-and-stick, have been applied to all three windows. He mentioned that the previous tenant had pink vinyl, which was removed. He stated he isn't sure which company installed the current vinyl but is primarily assisting in obtaining the necessary permit.

Mr. O’Keefe mentioned not having a picture showing the sign above the window that was previously approved by the board. Ms. Abaied pulled up last month's approval for Panda Dumpling to allow the board to see it all together. The main concern is that the green color of the sign doesn't fit with the overall color scheme. Mr. O’Keefe feels that the sign for Panda Dumpling should match the color theme, and if the sign had a combination of red, gray or black like the Panda Dumpling logo, he would be more satisfied with it.

Ms. Hanley asked for an explanation as to why the neon green color was chosen. Daniel responded that pandas eat bamboo, and they selected the neon green color to represent that. Ms. Couchman asked if the design be replaced with bamboo, or could bamboo be incorporated into the sign to help people make the connection.

Mr. Byars said he would talk to their graphic designer to explore options for the design. He suggests the possibility of incorporating bamboo into the background and using a darker green color, or alternatively, getting rid of the green entirely if preferred. Ms. Couchman expressed uncertainty about whether people will make the connection between the bamboo and the panda. She doesn’t want the applicant to spend money on creating multiple versions of the sign if the connection isn't clear. She suggests using one of the existing colors from the Panda sign to ensure better recognition and a clearer connection.

Ms. Hanley discussed the options for moving forward with a design application. She mentioned that the application can either be deferred for further revisions or voted on immediately. She suggests considering a new approach, such as making the design entirely a bamboo pattern. Another concern raised is the color choice, particularly the neon green, which doesn't harmonize with the logos or the neighboring businesses in the same building. She noted that any color combination matching the approved signage colors would be perfectly acceptable. The board discussed. 

Mr. Penati made a motion to defer the window signs for Panda Dumpling, located at 155 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1615945, in the AC, Avenue Center zoning district, filed by James Byars of Signs by James, LLC.

Motion: Mr. Penati 
Second: Mr. O’Keefe 
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 155 Maple Ave W - Panda Dumpling - Sign

Item No. 4: Request approval for exterior modifications, stormwater basin, located at 900 Follin Ln SE, Docket No. PF-1525485-BAR, in the CP, Corporate Park Zoning district, filed by Katie Moffat, Wetland Studies and Solutions, Inc, project contact.

Applicant present: Katie Moffatt

The applicant presented the project for the Navy Federal Credit Union campus, noting this is her second time presenting. The proposal involves replacing much of the turf with native vegetation, flattening the steep grade along the entrance, and adding a cobble-lined swale through the middle. The project is simple, with a previously conceptual planting plan now finalized, including specific plant types and locations.

Ms. Couhcman discussed plant selection for the site, mentioning that some compact Inquiry Hollies and boxwoods are being removed to access the area. She suggests replacing the plants with alternatives, such as Korean boxwoods or different varieties of viburnum, like the "Totem." She offered suggestions for diversifying the plant types, mentioning specific cultivars of Plethora, such as the Ruby Spice (pink) and white varieties. However, they note that one-gallon Plethora plants are quite small and suggest using larger sizes, like three-gallon plants, depending on the budget. 

Ms. Couchman made a motion to approve the exterior modifications of, the stormwater basin, located at 900 Follin Ln SE, Docket No. PF-1525485-BAR, in the CP, Corporate Park Zoning district, filed by Katie Moffat, Wetland Studies and Solutions, Inc., with the recommendation that Wetland Studies and Solutions take into consideration forthcoming comments on plant selection and sizes. 

Motion: Ms. Couchman
Second: Mr. O’Keefe 
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 900 Follin Ln SE - Navy Federal Credit Union - Exterior Modification

EventItemActionText:
Item No. 5: Request approval for exterior modifications, landscaping & wetland site, located at 1007 Electric Avenue SE, Docket No. PF-1525189-BAR, in the CP, Corporate Park Zoning district, filed by Katie Moffat, Wetland Studies and Solutions, Inc., project contact.

Applicant present: Katie Moffatt

Ms. Moffatt stated that the project involves enhancing an existing wetland that is currently flat and covered with invasive species. The plan is to create micro-topography to increase water pooling and replace invasive species with mostly native plants while removing a few species for access. The plant palette will be expanded to include various native species. A small boardwalk will be added to encourage people on campus to enjoy the space, with a few trees placed along the boardwalk to frame the area. Additionally, a seating mix (without woody plants) will be installed under the power lines. Existing flagstone pavers will mark the entrance to the boardwalk, and structures will be included to help manage erosion.

Ms. Shelly asked if the boardwalk was ADA accessible to which the applicant responded that the boardwalk is not considered ADA accessible due to the steep grade leading down to it and the use of flagstone, which makes it unfeasible to meet ADA standards.

Ms. Hanley asked if dogs visited the area. Ms. Moffatt said that the area is not commonly frequented by dogs, as it's primarily used by employees, though there could be occasional dog walkers from nearby houses. While the space is secluded and near a bike trail, making it susceptible to disturbances, efforts are being made to improve its appearance. The presence of shrubs may help deter dogs from running through the site. As for wildlife, the area has foxes near a stormwater basin, but the exact wildlife presence in the broader area is unclear.

Ms. Couchman suggested using at least three-gallon shrubs for the planting plan, recommending Inkberry Hollies and IKEA, which have performed well in Vienna due to their adaptability to wet, dry, and varied conditions. She also highlighted Clethra as another reliable choice. Regarding the replacement of a crepe myrtle, she suggested alternatives like a white fringe, serviceberry, or witch hazel, which would be more in line with the native feel and offer ornamental value.

Mr. O’Keefe made a motion to approve the exterior modifications, landscaping & wetland site, located at 1007 Electric Avenue SE, Docket No. PF-1525189-BAR, in the CP, Corporate Park Zoning district, filed by Katie Moffat, Wetland Studies and Solutions, Inc., as submitted. 

Motion: Mr. O’Keefe
Second: Mr. Penati 
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 1007 Electric Avenue SE - Navy Federal Credit Union - Exterior Modification

Item No. 6: Request for approval of a wall sign for Chef Tan, located at 132 Branch Rd SE, Docket No. PF-1512408, in the AE, Avenue East zoning district, filed by Nate Akey of Interagency, project contact.

Applicants present: Albert Yang, O Yang Yu, and Anthony Chang. 

Mr. Chang stated that Chef Tan is a restaurant expanding from New Jersey, New York, and Boston, with its first location in the Mid-Atlantic. The lease they signed had specific signage requirements, and as an eager new business in Vienna, they proactively installed the signage. The purpose of the meeting is to address any concerns regarding the installation.

Ms. Hanley emphasized that they are not compliance experts but want to ensure businesses are aware of the requirements, so future issues are addressed proactively. The board discussed how the sign appeared harmonious with a nice pop.

Item No. 7: Request approval for removal of a shed and installation of two walk-in coolers at 132 Branch Rd SE, Docket No. PF-1512377-BAR, in the AE, Avenue East Commercial Zoning district, filed by Nate Akey of Interagency, project contact.

Applicants present: Albert Yang, O Yang Yu, and Anthony Chang. 

The applicant stated that the request is to remove a shed by the previous tenant and replace it with two walk-in coolers to expand the storage area for the new kitchen. Coordination with the planning department has already been done to ensure the coolers won't block emergency vehicle access or emergency lighting.

Ms. Hanley raised concerns about inconsistencies in the application, specifically regarding the concrete pad. The document mentions a 2-inch pad, while the pictures and the staff report indicate a 5-inch pad, as the 2-inch would likely be insufficient. The applicant confirmed that it was 5 inches. 

Ms. Hanley questioned whether the installation complies with the approved site plan, which shows the structure 5 feet off the wall. From the picture, it appears to be closer. The speaker also notes the presence of gas meters on the right and wants to ensure it’s not problematic to be that close to the wall. They have asked staff to check if a modification is needed. The applicant responded that the issue has been noticed, and the general contractor has already been contacted to move the cooler 2 feet outward to ensure there is enough maneuvering space between the cooler and the wall.

Ms. Hanley notes that if the door is 2 feet and there's a 7-foot 4-inch space, there should be no conflict. However, the poured pads in the picture appeared to be closer to 4 or 5 feet, which could cause a conflict and potentially damage the doors if two people were inside. The applicant confirmed that the general contractor was contacted to shift the pad and cooler.

Ms. Hanley suggested considering a bollard in front of the cooler for protection. The discussion continued and the applicant agreed, recognizing that a bollard would indeed protect the cooler, and acknowledged it as a good idea that makes sense. 

Mr. O’Keefe made a motion to approve the request for the removal of a shed and installation of two walk-in coolers at 132 Branch Rd SE, Docket No. PF-1512377-BAR, in the AE, Avenue East Commercial Zoning district, filed by Nate Akey of Interagency, with the recommendation that a bollard be installed to protect the cooler from traffic.

Motion: Mr. O’Keefe
Second: Mr. Penati

The applicant was informed that if they chose to install the bollard, they should contact the town engineer before completing the project and submit a request for a minor site modification.
EventItemTitle: 132 Branch Rd SE - Chef Tan - Exterior Modifications

Item No. 8: Request for approval of wall signs, window signs and a replacement panel for the monument sign for Train, located at 352 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1609277, in the AW, Avenue West zoning district, filed by Paul Daniel, Ace Signs LLC, project contact.

Applicants present: Paul Daniel 
Mr. Daniel stated the proposal that includes four signs: three wall signs and one freestanding sign.

1. Front Elevation Sign: Replace the existing sign face with a new metal plate featuring 3-inch-deep channel letters in black and white.

2.Awning Signs: Replace two existing awning signs with new sign boxes, similar to those used by a previous tenant, to address sun fading and wind damage.

3.Freestanding Sign: Replace the existing freestanding sign with a new face while maintaining the same size.
The design is minimalistic and aligns with signage used at another location in McLean. Samples have been provided for reference.

Ms. Abaied noted that additional window signs were included in the application for awareness, though some fell under the 1.5 square-foot threshold. However, the signs on the west side and front are part of the application because they slightly exceed this size limit.

There was a discussion about the building's architectural inconsistencies, particularly the contrast between the front and side elevations. The existing Greco-Roman columns on the side create a visual disconnect, and while the current awnings complement them, the proposed signage does not necessarily enhance the design.
Two options were considered:

1. Lighted Sign Boxes (Preferred by the Business Owner): 6-inch deep boxes with acrylic faces and vinyl graphics.

2. Awning Signs (Not Lighted): Positioned at a different angle from the previous awnings.
The preference is for the lighted sign boxes, while the awning option was not well received. There was also a broader desire to improve the building’s overall aesthetic beyond signage.

Mr. Penati made a motion to approve the request for wall signs, window signs and a replacement panel for the monument sign for Train, located at 352 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1609277, in the AW, Avenue West zoning district, filed by Paul Daniel, Ace Signs LLC, as submitted (Lighted Sign Boxes). 

Motion: Mr. Penati
Second: Mr. O’Keefe 
Motion Carried

Item No. 9: Request approval of installation of a new exterior door and light and removal of awnings, located at 352 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1604266-BAR, in the AW, Avenue West Commercial Zoning district, filed by Scot Loiselle, Onyx Creative, project contact.

Applicants present: Marie Johnson 

Ms. Johnson presented the following proposed exterior modifications for Train: 
1. New Rear Exterior Door: A 3’ x 7’ hollow metal door with a matching Sherwin-Williams Oyster Bar (7565) finish. This door would improve access for clients and staff, allowing easier movement to the dumpsters and reducing disruption inside the training facility.

2. New Light Fixture: A wall-mounted light (8.75” W x 5.75” H x 11” D) installed 10 feet above the new door to provide illumination while minimizing impact on neighboring properties.

3. Awning Removal & Facade Restoration: The existing awnings will be removed and replaced with lighted sign boxes, with full restoration of the building facade to ensure a clean and finished appearance.
After the applicant's presentation, it was noted that the lighting standard is typically limited to 2700–3000 Kelvin for a more visually pleasing effect, especially near residential areas. The proposed fixture is acceptable, but a lower Kelvin option is preferred.

Ms. Hanley commented on the existing floodlight on the corner of the building.  While it cannot be required to change, she strongly recommended that the fixture be updated to comply with Dark Sky standards by lowering Kelvin levels and ensuring appropriate lumens. The fixture above the right-hand corner windows is likely not energy-efficient, so upgrading it would be beneficial.

The discussion shifted to the visual inconsistency between the side and front of the building. While no changes are required due to existing conditions, the mismatched Greco-Roman columns were noted as a potential area for future improvement.

An opportunity was identified in front of the side entrance, where a large area of yellow striping exists. The tenant might consider repurposing it in the future potentially as a patio or another functional space since it is not designated for parking. 

Mr. O’Keefe made a motion to approve the installation of a new exterior door and light and the removal of awnings, located at 352 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1604266-BAR, in the AW, Avenue West Commercial Zoning district, filed by Scot Loiselle, Onyx Creative, as submitted and with the recommendation to replace the flood light with a dark sky-compliant fixture, and with the condition that the proposed light be replaced with a similar fixture not to exceed 3,000 Kelvin.

Motion: O’Keefe
Second: Ms. Couchman
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 352 Maple Ave W - Train - Exterior Modifications

Item No. 10: Request for approval of string lights for Cafe De Vienna, located at 131 Church St NW, Docket No. PF-1217390-BAR, in the CS, Church Street zoning district, filed by Reza Sadeghi, Toranj LLC, project contact.

Applicants present : Reza Sadeghi

The applicant Reza Sedeji, owner of Café de Vienna, discussed the patio lighting installation. The lights are 2-watt LED string lights mounted along the patio perimeter, anchored to the wall, a pole, and an exterior sign using high-strength aircraft cable with a 250 lb pull strength. The total weight of the lights is approximately 38.5 lbs with anchor points reducing stress.

The lights are turned on in the afternoon but shut off by 7:00 PM as the café closes. During summer, they may not be used at all since they serve more for ambiance rather than illumination.

The question was raised about the need for lights if the café isn’t open in the evening. The applicant explained that the lights are part of the café's image, though they aren't positioned around the seating area, which makes them look awkward. He noted that running the lights from the building's wall helps illuminate the shrubbery.

Mr. Sadeghi also mentioned the challenge of installing posts for the lights, as the building is nearly 140 years old and has complex utilities, including an unknown metal pipe coming from the basement. To avoid disturbing these utilities, he opted not to install posts and instead anchored the lights to the wall. He clarified that the lighting is part of the café's image, aiming to create a cozy, old-fashioned look like typical cafes with hanging lights. While the café isn't open late, the lights are used to maintain this aesthetic, especially when the weather is good. In winter, they are turned off if it's too cold or if there is no outdoor seating. The lights also help brighten the area, as the side of the building is otherwise very dark at night. He emphasized that the goal is simply the look and feel of the café, without making drastic changes to the building’s appearance.

Ms. Couchman voiced her concern about how allowing string lights could set a precedent for other businesses to install them without clear guidelines. She suggested being more intentional with the placement of lights, such as securing them around the patio perimeter and possibly using buried conduits for better organization. The goal is to avoid a trend where string lights are used haphazardly, which could complicate future applications. 

The applicant explained that he doesn't want to overdo the lighting on the café's patio, as the building is old, and he aims to preserve its original character. The goal is not to make a grand statement or advertise but to provide some visibility outside, as there is no exterior lighting. He mentioned that the area is quite dark at night, and the lights are simply for aesthetic purposes, not for bright illumination. He emphasized that if the lighting isn't approved, he will remove it, as it currently has minimal impact. The café is set back from the street, with most neighboring businesses being much closer.

Ms. Couchman suggested considering alternatives to the string lights, such as installing path lights along the walk or using twinkle lights under umbrellas. The goal was to find a more structured alternative to the current lighting setup. The board suggested focusing the lighting over the patio only, without visually connecting it to the building. This would add a quaint look to the patio and building. Instead of using additional posts, the proposal is to utilize the existing structures and either run conduit or the current wire system to power the lights, using the tension pole to stabilize the setup. This approach aims to keep the lighting less visually intrusive. 

The discussion focused on finding a compromise for the lighting setup. The tension wire could be replaced with a conduit buried underground to power the lights. There was concern over the visual appearance of the current post, with suggestions to paint it black or plant a climbing vine. The consensus was to remove the lights from one side, paint the post black, and use conduit to power lights on two sides of the patio. The applicant  was open to removing the lighting if it was deemed non-compliant but expressed a desire to create ambiance with other low-cost options like solar lights.

Ms. Couchman made a motion to deny the request for approval of string lights for Cafe De Vienna, located at 131 Church St NW, Docket No. PF-1217390-BAR, in the CS, Church Street zoning district, filed by Reza Sadeghi, Toranj LLC, project contact.

The applicant was informed he can bring forward other options if he feels lights are critical to the ambiance of his business. 

Motion: Ms. Couhcman 
Second: 
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 131 Church St NW - Café de Vienna - Exterior Modification - Revision

Item #2 was recalled- Request for approval of a wall sign, vinyl window clings, and a secondary sign for Clarity, located at 442 Maple Ave E, Docket No. PF-155195, in the AE, Avenue East zoning district, filed by Burton Francois, BeBold Sign Studio, project contact.

There were concerns about the signage and its placement, suggesting that the sign should be turned to face a different direction for better visibility. The board expressed issues with the inconsistency in the building's signs, particularly with color clashes, and the lack of a clear entrance. They recommend adjustments to improve the building’s visual harmony, particularly with a possible entrance arch. 

Ms. Couchman made a motion to defer the request for a wall sign, vinyl window clings, and a secondary sign for Clarity, located at 442 Maple Ave E, Docket No. PF-155195, in the AE, Avenue East zoning district, filed by Burton Francois, BeBold Sign Studio, until the applicant can attend the meeting.
